https://www.budapesttimes.hu/hungary/the.text: The Budapest Times The tolls of a new era: Mészáros fund repays billions after road deal review Around 2.27 billion forints have been repaid to the state by Prime Tech Magántőkealap, a private equity fund linked to Lőrinc Mészáros, following a review of an earlier transaction related to the electronic road toll system — Transportation and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy announced in a Facebook post on Saturday. The previous government, during the tenure of Minister János Lázár, purchased three key players in the electronic road toll system for 64.5 billion forints in late 2025 and in January of this year: Kupon Portfólió Kft., Setech Flotta Kft., and i-Cell Mobilsoft Zrt. Kupon Portfólió and Setech Flotta had previously been owned by Prime Tech Magántőkealap, which the press identified as an investment fund linked to Lőrinc Mészáros, the minister wrote. The due diligence conducted on the transaction revealed that, under the sales contract for Kupon Portfólió, the company’s 2025 profit would still have been due to the previous owner, who had already drawn a dividend advance of 2.27 billion forints. Dávid Vitézy pointed out that this was not accepted, and the now state-owned company took legal action, demanding that the former owner repay the dividend advance. The amount arrived on 5 August 2026, meaning that the 2.27 billion forints ultimately remained not with the former owner but in the retained earnings of the state-owned company. He said that in recent years, too many contracts had been signed in the transport sector whose primary beneficiaries were not passengers, not carriers, and not Hungarian taxpayers, but a narrow economic circle. That is why a comprehensive audit had been launched into the operations of background institutions and state transport companies, the minister explained, adding that they are reviewing every transaction in which there is reason to believe that public funds were not managed in the interest of the Hungarian people. Where there is suspicion of a legal violation, the necessary legal steps will be taken, and where possible, the money of Hungarian taxpayers will be recovered. What we know on day 1,675 Guardian staff and agencies Thu 24 Sep 2026 20.20 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Finnish President Alexander Stubb has said he pleaded with SpaceX owner Elon Musk to expand Starlink satellite internet coverage for Ukraine so it can strike Russian ballistic missile launchers located inside ⁠Russian territory. Ukraine ⁠has an acute shortage ​of air defences to repel Russian ballistic missiles and Kyiv believes that turning on Starlink over Russian territory would help it target the launchers that fire the missiles. Musk switched on the Starlink satellite internet service over ‌Ukraine shortly after Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022. It has become the lifeblood of Ukraine’s battlefield communications and a tool for piloting drones, but it does not work over Russian territory. Volodymyr Zelenskyy has met with senior Wall Street executives on ​the sidelines of the UN general assembly in New York , ⁠as Kyiv seeks to attract investments to help finance the country’s rebuilding efforts. The meeting focused mainly ⁠on areas such as helping Ukraine get through the winter and supporting its economy, the Ukrainian ⁠government said. Ukraine faces a brutal winter as stepped-up Russian strikes on ​its infrastructure and key ‌export industries deepen ‌the country’s budget crisis. The daily cost of the war ‌grew to about $190m this year. The meeting, attended by more than two dozen US companies, was facilitated by US banking giant Citigroup and the US chamber of commerce. Russia could launch a limited military attack against a Nato country in the coming months, Danish intelligence said , in one of the starkest warnings yet by western security services . In a report published on Thursday, the Danish defence intelligence service warned of a “low but growing risk” that Russia could launch long-range strikes on Nato infrastructure supporting Ukraine, or carry out a limited incursion into a neighbouring country with a small number of troops, potentially operating without insignia. The report came hours after a fire at a Starlink satellite station in central Poland that local authorities described as an “act of sabotage”. Nato is capable of handling sabotage and drone incidents in Europe and has good action plans in place to deal with them , the alliance’s secretary general said after the warning from Danish intelligence. Secretary-general Mark Rutte said he believes the rising number of hybrid incidents in Nato countries shows that Russian President Vladimir Putin is losing the war in Ukraine. He said that citizens of the 32 Nato countries can remain calm. “Putin is in a bad place,” Rutte said. “He is not winning the war in Ukraine.” Russian drone and missile strikes on Kyiv and Ukraine’s north-east killed eight people on ⁠Thursday in attacks that included ⁠a maternity hospital and a ​farm , officials said. Two people died ⁠in the assault on Kyiv, Zelenskyy said. “As people were sleeping, flashes from explosions lit up the sky,” the president said on Telegram. Police said nine homes, a post office, ​warehouses and dozens of cars were also damaged in Kyiv. A separate ‌Russian attack on a vegetable storage ‌facility at a farm in a village of the north-eastern Kharkiv region killed six people and injured a further 12, prosecutors said. ⁠Turkish president Tayyip Erdogan said Turkey ⁠had ⁠stepped up ​efforts to re-establish the Black ⁠Sea grain corridor . “We have now increased ⁠our efforts to ​re-establish ‌the grain corridor. ‌We are also ‌accelerating our diplomatic steps for this,” Erdogan told a group of Turkish journalists ‌in New York. Erdogan said ⁠he had discussed ​the ​issue again ​with Zelenskyy ‌and received ​a ​positive response. Photograph: Evan Vucci/Reuters Donald Trump Trump backs away from top aides who reportedly advised pro-Russia government President floats firing Chris LaCivita and James Blair over any ‘conflict’ after reports of work in Republika Srpska Ariana Baio Wed 7 Oct 2026 16.31 EDT Last modified on Wed 7 Oct 2026 18.07 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Donald Trump distanced himself from two top advisers on Wednesday, claiming he did not have “any idea who else they work for”, after it was reported they spent the weekend assisting a pro-Russia government in the Balkans. On Truth Social, Trump wrote that Chris LaCivita , the co-manager of his 2024 presidential campaign, and James Blair, a campaign adviser and White House deputy chief of staff on leave of absence, “are outside consultants” and “do not work for me other than as outside consultants”. “They are allowed to do work for others, just like all consultants in Washington, D.C.,” Trump wrote. “I do not have any idea who else they work for but will, on reflection, ask them and, if there’s a conflict, I will terminate them, immediately!” The president’s comments came after the New York Times reported that LaCivita and Blair traveled to Republika Srpska, an autonomous entity in Bosnia and Herzegovina, to assist the government ahead of elections over the weekend. Sources told the newspaper that each adviser was paid hundreds of thousands of dollars. LaCivita and Blair are meanwhile working with Maga Inc , the Trump-backed SuperPac assisting Republican candidates in November’s US midterm elections. Both men have long histories with Trump , and the US president has praised them separately on social media. LaCivita joined Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign in 2022, after leading a pro-Trump Super Pac called Preserve America. In 2024, Trump wrote on Truth Social that LaCivita was “ THE BEST ” co-campaign manager alongside Susie Wiles, who now serves as White House chief of staff. Blair worked for Trump’s 2020 campaign in Florida and was the political director of Trump’s 2024 campaign. He joined the president at the White House as deputy chief of staff for legislative, political and public affairs. In April, Trump called Blair “ one of the brightest political minds ” while announcing that Blair would leave his White House position, briefly, to join Maga Inc and assist Republicans in the midterms. Trump said Blair would return to the White House after the midterms. Trump’s statement distancing himself from the two advisers comes as Maga Inc prepares to ramp up efforts to assist Republican candidates in next month’s elections. Public polls indicate Democrats are leading Republicans in several key competitive races . That is largely attributed to widespread disapproval over Trump’s handling of the economy and cost of living. A spokesperson for Maga Inc told the New York Times that Blair and LaCivita remained engaged with midterm efforts while traveling, saying the two “hosted a team call with race captains on Saturday morning to go over recent survey data”. The Guardian has contacted Maga Inc for comment. Despite polling showing waning voter enthusiasm for Republicans, the party has a cash advantage over Democrats. At the end of August, Maga Inc had more than $415m cash on hand. Several Super Pacs tied to Maga Inc have begun launching multimillion-dollar ad blitzes.
